hospitals.description: Golisano Children's Hospital is the pediatric hospital of the University of Rochester Medical Center, built as an eight floor tower attached to Strong Memorial Hospital on the university's south campus off Elmwood Avenue. It is the referral center for seriously ill and injured children across a 17 county Finger Lakes region and runs the only Level IV NICU in that region (68 beds), a regional PICU, a pediatric emergency department that sees more than 32,000 children a year, and the only pediatric cardiac surgery program in Western New York. The current building opened in two phases in 2015 and 2017, the second phase adding pediatric operating rooms and a new PICU, and it houses a Ronald McDonald House inside the hospital. More than 200 pediatric faculty work across 40 plus specialties, and U.S. News ranks it nationally in several pediatric specialties. Rochester is a mid size, affordable city on Lake Ontario, and the hospital sits a few minutes from downtown and the Genesee River.
highlights: Only Level IV NICU in the Finger Lakes region (68 beds, about 1,200 admissions a year)
ACS verified Level I pediatric trauma center, one of eight pediatric trauma hospitals of that level in New York
Only pediatric cardiac surgery program in Western New York
Largest pediatric intensive care service in Western New York, about 1,000 PICU admissions a year
Ranked by U.S. News in 8 of 11 pediatric specialties per the hospital's quick facts page
Over 32,000 pediatric emergency visits a year; 17 county referral region
New tower completed in 2017 with Ronald McDonald House inside the hospital
hospitals.notes: Parent Strong Memorial Hospital (886 beds, Level I adult trauma) is not listed separately; pediatric postings appear under Strong Memorial or Golisano Children's on the UR Workday boards. Bed counts differ by source: the hospital quick facts page lists 148 beds, Wikipedia lists 190 (168 private pediatric beds). The URMC PICU page describes a 12 bed unit on 6 North, which may predate the 2017 PICU expansion. NYS DOH lists Strong as a Regional Perinatal Center with PICU beds. UR Medicine also owns Highland Hospital, Jones Memorial (Wellsville) and other affiliates.

hospitals.description: Upstate Golisano Children's Hospital is the pediatric hospital of SUNY Upstate Medical University, occupying the tower of Upstate University Hospital on University Hill in Syracuse. It serves 22 counties of Central New York plus parts of Pennsylvania and Vermont with 71 private pediatric rooms, including a 15 bed PICU on the 12th floor and a 12 bed hematology/oncology unit, plus an 11 bed biobehavioral health unit. It runs the only dedicated pediatric emergency department between Rochester and Vermont, is an ACS verified Level I pediatric trauma center, and shares the region's only burn center and the Upstate New York Poison Center. Newborn intensive care for the region is provided next door at Crouse Hospital, which is connected by a bridge and tunnel. The campus sits beside Syracuse University, a short drive from downtown and the Finger Lakes.
highlights: Only dedicated pediatric emergency department between Rochester and Vermont
ACS verified Level I pediatric trauma center with the region's only burn center (Clark Burn Center)
15 bed PICU serving a 17 county critical care region
71 pediatric beds plus an 11 bed biobehavioral health unit
Pediatric hospitalist service admits more than 3,000 patients a year
Parent hospital is ANCC Magnet (since January 2021) and the region's only adult Level I trauma center

wikipedia.title: Upstate University Hospital
wikipedia.extract: Upstate University Hospital is a 752-bed non-profit, teaching hospital located in Syracuse, New York. Upstate University Hospital is the flagship hospital of the Upstate Health System. As the hospital is a teaching hospital, it is affiliated with the Norton College of Medicine at State University of New York Upstate Medical University. The hospital is also an American College of Surgeons verified Level 1 Trauma Center, the only in the region and one of 21 in New York. Attached to the hospital is the Upstate Golisano Children's Hospital that treats infants, children, teens, and young adults aged 0–21.

hospitals.description: Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo, known until January 2026 as John R. Oishei Children's Hospital, is Western New York's freestanding children's hospital and part of Kaleida Health. The 12 story building opened in November 2017 on the Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus downtown and has about 185 inpatient beds. It is an ACS verified Level I pediatric trauma center, runs a 64 bed Level IV NICU and a 20 bed PICU, and is recognized as an ECMO center of excellence by the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization. It is the main pediatric teaching hospital for the University at Buffalo, and a $50 million gift from Tom Golisano in 2025 led to the new name. The medical campus sits at the edge of downtown Buffalo near Allentown and the Elmwood Village.
highlights: Freestanding children's hospital for Western New York, opened November 2017
ACS verified Level I pediatric trauma center, one of six in New York State per UB
64 bed Level IV NICU and 20 bed PICU
Renamed January 2026 after a $50 million Golisano gift, the largest in Kaleida's history
University at Buffalo pediatric teaching hospital; around 28,000 admissions a year per UB
hospitals.notes: Postings may still say Oishei or OCH. Wikipedia infobox lists 197 beds vs 185 in the article text. NYS DOH lists it (as Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo) as a Regional Perinatal Center with pediatric, PICU and NICU beds. Kaleida's Buffalo General Medical Center is attached on the same campus (adult only).

wikipedia.title: Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo
wikipedia.extract:
Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo, formerly known as John R. Oishei Children's Hospital, is a women's and children's hospital in Buffalo, New York, that opened on November 10, 2017.  It provides pediatric specialties and subspecialties to infants, children, teens, and young adults up to age 21, and maternity services for expectant mothers. It is located at the Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus and has 185 inpatient beds. It is a pediatric facility serving patients in Western New York and parts of Southern Ontario. The hospital is one of the only freestanding children's hospitals in New York State. Golisano Children's Hospital is a teaching hospital affiliated with the State University of New York at Buffalo and is affiliated with the Kaleida Health System.
The hospital contains an ACS verified level 1 pediatric trauma center, one of the few in the region. Golisano Children's Hospital also has a rooftop helipad to transport critically ill patients to and from the hospital.
The hospital was originally named after the John R. Oishei Foundation, which donated $10 million for the development of the hospital.  
In January 2026, the hospital was renamed Golisano Children's Hospital of Buffalo.
